laws.name: Lag (2001:82) om svenskt medborgarskap
laws.articles: 2 § (birth), 14 § (loss at 22 and regaining), 21 § (declaration), transitional provisions of Lag (2014:481); amended up to SFS 2026:1689, major reform Lag (2026:447) in force 6 June 2026
laws.quote: 2 § Ett barn förvärvar svenskt medborgarskap vid födelsen, om 1. en förälder till barnet är svensk medborgare, eller 2. en avliden förälder till barnet var svensk medborgare vid sin död. Lag (2014:481). [EN: A child acquires Swedish citizenship at birth if 1. a parent of the child is a Swedish citizen, or 2. a deceased parent of the child was a Swedish citizen at death.]

rules.rule: Born on or after 1 April 2015 anywhere to a parent who is Swedish at the time of birth (or a deceased parent who was Swedish at death): Swedish at birth, automatically. Only the parent's citizenship at the child's birth counts; no route through grandparents unless the parent was still Swedish when the child was born.
rules.quote: A child born after 1 April 2015 always acquires Swedish citizenship if any of the following applies to you: Either of their parents is a Swedish citizen at the time of the child’s birth. A deceased parent of the child was a Swedish citizen at the time of their death. This applies regardless of the country in which the child is born.

rules.rule: Born 1 July 2001 - 31 March 2015: Swedish at birth if the mother was Swedish (anywhere), or the father was Swedish and either the child was born in Sweden or the father was married to the mother. Born abroad to an unmarried Swedish father: not automatic; became Swedish if the parents later married while the child was under 18 and unmarried ('legitimation'); otherwise only by the father's notification before the child turns 18.
rules.quote: Children with a Swedish mother A child with a Swedish mother always became a Swedish citizen. It did not matter if the child was born in Sweden or abroad. Children with a Swedish father and a non-Swedish mother A child of a Swedish father and a non-Swedish mother always became a Swedish citizen if the child was born in Sweden. If their father was married to their mother, the child acquired Swedish citizenship at birth, regardless of where in the world the child was born. [...] Prior to 1 April 2015, children with a Swedish father who were born abroad did not automatically receive Swedish citizenship. In order for the child to be granted Swedish citizenship, the father needs to file a notification.

rules.rule: Child born out of wedlock outside Sweden before 1 April 2015 to a Swedish father: the FATHER files a notification while the child is under 18; father must have been Swedish at the birth; paternity validly established; all guardians approve; child 12+ consents; extra identity/criminal-record conditions from 15. Still available after the 6 June 2026 reform. Once the child is 18 this route is closed.
rules.quote: The child must be less than 18 years old The father must have been a Swedish citizen at the time of the child’s birth Paternity must have been established in a valid manner [...] It is the child’s father who must file a notification of citizenship for the child. If the child has more than one parent/legal guardian, all their parents/legal guardians must approve the notification. Children who have reached the age of 12 must consent to become a Swedish citizen by signing the notification.

rules.rule: A Swedish citizen born abroad who has never had residence (hemvist) in Sweden and has not stayed in Sweden in circumstances showing ties (e.g. a lengthy stay or regular shorter visits) loses citizenship automatically on the 22nd birthday, unless an application to retain is filed after 18 and before 22 (free; at an embassy/consulate). No loss if it would cause statelessness or after 7+ years total residence in Denmark/Finland/Iceland/Norway. When a parent loses citizenship this way, children who derived it from that parent lose it too, unless they also derive it from the other parent who is still Swedish.
rules.quote: 14 § En svensk medborgare förlorar sitt svenska medborgarskap när han eller hon fyller tjugotvå år, om han eller hon 1. är född utomlands, 2. aldrig haft hemvist i Sverige, och 3. inte heller varit här under förhållanden som tyder på samhörighet med landet. På ansökan som görs innan den svenske medborgaren fyller tjugotvå år får dock medges att medborgarskapet behålls. Den som har förlorat sitt svenska medborgarskap enligt första stycket får efter ansökan medges att medborgarskapet återfås med verkan från den tidpunkt då medborgarskapet förlorades. När någon förlorar svenskt medborgarskap enligt första stycket, förlorar även hans eller hennes barn sitt svenska medborgarskap, om barnet förvärvat detta på grund av att föräldern varit svensk medborgare. [...] Lag (2026:447). [EN: A Swedish citizen loses Swedish citizenship on turning 22 if born abroad, has never been resident in Sweden, and has not stayed here in circumstances indicating ties to the country. On application made before turning 22, retention may be granted. A person who has lost citizenship under the first paragraph may on application be allowed to regain it with effect from the time of loss. When someone loses citizenship under the first paragraph, their child also loses it if the child acquired it because that parent was Swedish.]

rules.rule: Practical retention test from Migrationsverket: apply between 18 and 22; no application needed if the person has lived in Sweden or regularly visited Sweden.
rules.quote: In this context, an “affinity” means that you have a connection to Sweden, for example that you have stayed here for a lengthy period, or regularly for several shorter periods, prior to turning 22 years old. [...] You must do this after you are 18 years old, but before you turn 22. You do not need to make such an application if you have lived in Sweden or if you have regularly visited Sweden.

rules.rule: NEW from 6 June 2026: a person who lost Swedish citizenship at 22 under § 14 may apply (from age 22, free, at an embassy/consulate) to regain it, effective from the 22nd birthday, if Migrationsverket finds the loss had disproportionate consequences under EU law for the person or family in Sweden or another EU state; only circumstances before age 22 count; relevant only for losses after 1 January 1995. A US-only life with no EU ties will rarely qualify.
rules.quote: We investigate the consequences of the loss of Swedish citizenship from an EU law perspective. For example, your family might be split up if you can no longer stay in a country once you are no longer an EU citizen. We base our assessment on what your situation was like up until your 22nd birthday. The EU law perspective is relevant if you lost your Swedish citizenship after 1 January 1995, the date on which Sweden joined the EU. You can submit your application once you have turned 22. If the Swedish Migration Agency decides to regain your Swedish citizenship, the decision will take effect from your 22nd birthday.

rules.rule: From 6 June 2026 the notification routes for former Swedish citizens and young adults (old §§ 7 and 9) are repealed (Lag 2026:447). A non-Nordic former Swedish citizen (e.g. lost citizenship on US naturalization before 1 July 2001) must now APPLY for citizenship and needs at least 2 years' residence in Sweden (plus the general conditions of the reformed law). Checker: former citizens living in the US have no remote route.
rules.quote: From 6 June, only adult Nordic citizens, stateless children and young adults born in Sweden will be able to apply for Swedish citizenship. A father who is a Swedish citizen will be able to submit a notification of a child born out of wedlock and outside Sweden before 1 April 2015. Everyone else must apply for Swedish citizenship. [...] 2 years if you are a Nordic citizen or a former Swedish citizen

rules.rule: If unsure whether one became Swedish at birth or lost it (born abroad, never lived in Sweden, naturalized elsewhere), apply for a free declaration of citizenship (medborgarskapsförklaring, form 322011) at an embassy/consulate.
rules.quote: If you do not know whether you have previously gained or lost Swedish citizenship, you can apply for a declaration of citizenship. For example, you can do this if you are unsure about any of the following: Did I become a Swedish citizen at birth? I was born abroad and have never lived in Sweden – have I lost my citizenship? I have acquired citizenship in another country – have I therefore lost my Swedish citizenship? [...] It costs nothing to apply for a declaration of citizenship.

procedure.authority: Migrationsverket (Swedish Migration Agency), Medborgarskapsenheten, Norrköping; applicants abroad file at a Swedish embassy or consulate-general; Skatteverket registers births abroad in the Population Register; passports via embassy or police
procedure.how: Child of a Swedish parent born abroad: register with Skatteverket and apply for a passport at the embassy. Before 22 (if no residence/ties in Sweden): file form 302021 'Ansökan om att få behålla svenskt medborgarskap' at the embassy. Unmarried Swedish father, child born abroad before 1 April 2015 and still under 18: father files form 321011 at the embassy (fee SEK 475). Doubt about status: free declaration (form 322011).

documents.item: Certificate of paternity, father's passport showing citizenship at the child's birth, custody decision (if applicable), child's birth certificate (if child lives abroad), child's ID (15+)
documents.note: Father notification route; all copies must be certified

documents.item: Identity document, birth certificate (if born out of wedlock), parents' marriage certificate
Correctly made passport copies; proof of Swedish citizenship if acquired by application/notification

fees.quote: It costs nothing to apply to retain your Swedish citizenship.

fees.quote: It costs nothing to apply for a declaration of citizenship.

dual_citizenship.note: Allowed since the 2001 Act entered into force on 1 July 2001; a Swedish citizen who naturalizes abroad keeps Swedish citizenship. Before 1 July 2001 (1950 Act) Swedes lost citizenship on voluntary naturalization abroad (date from the Act's entry into force; the old loss rule itself not quoted from an official page).
dual_citizenship.quote: Sweden allows dual and multiple citizenship. [...] A Swedish citizen who becomes a citizen of another country may retain their Swedish citizenship. However, some countries’ legislation does not allow dual citizenship.

other_requirements.item: Act of 2001 entry into force (start of dual citizenship regime)
other_requirements.quote: 1. Denna lag träder i kraft den 1 juli 2001, då lagen (1950:382) om svenskt medborgarskap skall upphöra att gälla.

recent_changes.what: Lag (2026:447) in force without transitional arrangements: residence for naturalization 8 years (2 for former Swedish citizens), self-support and Swedish language/society knowledge requirements, citizenship test from August 2026; notification routes limited to adult Nordic citizens, stateless children/young adults born in Sweden and Swedish fathers of children born abroad out of wedlock before 1 April 2015; former-citizen notification (old § 9) repealed; new possibility to regain citizenship lost at 22 (EU-law proportionality).
Exemptions from the permanent residence permit requirement for citizenship (SFS 2026:1689; news item 2026-07-12 seen on Migrationsverket pages). Not relevant to descent claims.
Migrationsverket news: the Swedish language test for citizenship may be postponed (knowledge can be shown in other ways meanwhile).

open_questions: Brief's 'SEK 175' fee not found anywhere; current official fees: retain 0, declaration 0, father notification SEK 475, regain-after-22 0, application SEK 2,900.

Children born abroad before 1 July 1979 to a Swedish mother married to a foreign father (1950 Act: mother transmitted only if unmarried or child born in Sweden), and the transitional notification routes of 1979/2001: Migrationsverket's current pages only describe rules from 1 July 2001; the pre-2001 rules were not confirmed on an official page. Route such users to the free declaration of citizenship.

Brief's '18-20 notification route for former citizens' was repealed on 6 June 2026 (§§ 7 and 9 'Har upphävts genom lag (2026:447)'). The transitional provisions of Lag 2026:447 are not printed in the Riksdagen consolidated text; whether notifications filed before 6 June 2026 are still decided under old rules was not confirmed.
Processing times for retention, declaration and regain applications are not published on their pages.

Pre-2001 loss on foreign naturalization: date of the dual-citizenship switch confirmed (Act in force 1 July 2001), but no official page quote found stating the old loss rule; Americans whose Swedish parent naturalized in the US before 1 July 2001 and before the child's birth were likely not born Swedish - verify per case via declaration.
